segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Okay, um.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Right, I think we're all here, so let's get started.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Uh, welcome everyone, this is our kickoff meeting.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: I'm Helen, I'll be the project manager for this one.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Mm-hmm.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: So the plan for today is, um, a quick round of introductions, then I'll explain the project, and then we'll talk about what each of you does before next time.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: So, um, Tom, do you want to start?

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Yeah, sure. I'm Tom, I'm the marketing expert.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: So I'll be looking at, uh, what the users want and what's out there already.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Okay.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Um, I'm Priya, user interface designer.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: So basically how people actually use the thing, the buttons, the display, that kind of stuff.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: And I'm Marcus, industrial designer.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Uh, so the inside of it really, the components, the casing, what it's made of.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Great.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Okay so, the project. We're designing a wearable step counter.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: And the, um, the target group is seniors. So older people, let's say sixty-five and up.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Okay.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: So like a pedometer basically?

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Yeah, a pedometer, but something you wear, so it should be, um, comfortable and easy to use for older people.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: That's actually quite a nice brief.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Management has given us some numbers.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Um, it should sell for thirty-five euros.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: And the production cost can't be more than fifteen euros per unit.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Fifteen. Okay.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Is that, um, is that per unit including the strap and everything?

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Yeah, the whole thing. Everything that goes in the box.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Right.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: That's tight but, uh, doable I think. Pedometer sensors are pretty cheap.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: And the market is, uh, international, so they want to sell it in Europe mainly.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Um.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: So before we split up, I thought we'd just do a quick first-impressions round.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: What do you think a step counter for seniors needs? Just off the top of your head.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Well, for me the first thing is the display.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Older people, a lot of them have trouble reading small text.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: So the numbers should be really big. Like, the step count should be the main thing you see.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Yeah.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Definitely, yeah. My grandmother can't read anything on her phone.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: So big numbers. Everyone agree on that?

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Yeah, absolutely.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Yeah.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Okay, so large display, readable numbers, that's a given then.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Um, and from my side, the question is where you wear it.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: I was thinking a clip, like you clip it on your belt or your waistband.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: That's actually where step counters are most accurate, near the hip.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Hmm, but a clip, if you—

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: I'm not sure about a clip. Older people might find it fiddly to put on.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: A wristband might be easier. You just put it on like a watch.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Yeah but then the counting is less reliable on the wrist, because you move your arms around.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Mm.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Okay, I think that's something we'll have to come back to.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Let's not decide that today. We can look at it properly in the next meeting.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Fair enough.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Uh, one thing I'd throw in, um.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: What about fall detection? Like, if someone falls it sends an alert.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: That's a big thing for seniors, and families would pay for that.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: That's a lot more than a step counter though.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: You'd need some kind of wireless connection, a phone link or something.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Yeah, I'm a bit worried about that with fifteen euros.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Let's park it for now. It's a good idea but I don't want us to commit to it yet.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Okay, yeah.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Um, so.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: I could look into what existing step counters for older people are like. What's already on the market, how they look, what the buttons are.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Actually, uh—

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: I think that's more of a marketing thing, the market research part.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: I'll take that, I'll do the competitor overview.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Oh, yeah, sure.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: That makes sense, go for it.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Yeah, that fits better with your role, Tom.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: So Tom, you look at the existing products for seniors, what's out there and what they cost.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Yep, will do.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: And Priya, you can focus on the interface then. The display, the buttons, how many functions.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Okay, yeah. I'll think about the functional side, what the user actually needs to press.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Great.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: And me, the components?

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Yeah, Marcus, could you look at the, um, the working design. What sensor, what battery, that kind of thing.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Sure, I'll look at that.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: And the clip versus wristband thing, I'll check what that means for the sensor.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Okay, good.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Um.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Batteries actually, that's a thing. Older people don't want to be charging stuff every night.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Mm-hmm.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Yeah, a coin battery that lasts a year would be ideal.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Right. And someone should probably check what the whole thing costs at some point, strap, packaging, all of it, so we know where we stand with the fifteen euros.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Mm.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Yeah.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Oh, and, um, do we have a name for it yet or anything?

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Not yet, no. That's for later.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Okay.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Okay, so, um, just to wrap up.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Next meeting is the functional design meeting.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: That's in about thirty minutes. You'll get, um, an email from me with some more info.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: I'll also send round the minutes from today.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Do we present something next time?

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Yeah, everyone does a short presentation on their part. Few slides, nothing fancy.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Okay.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Should we, uh, decide anything on the clip before then or?

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: No, just bring what you find and we'll discuss it together.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Right.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: I might bring a couple of sketches of the display. Just rough ones.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: That would be great, yeah.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: As long as it doesn't count the steps to the fridge. My uncle would never wear it.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Ha, that'd be me as well.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Okay, um.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Is everyone clear on what they're doing?

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Yep.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Yeah.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Yeah, all good.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: So just to recap: Tom, existing products. Priya, interface. Marcus, components and the clip question.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: And the big display, we've agreed on that.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Mm-hmm.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Okay. Thanks everyone, see you in half an hour.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Cheers.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Thanks.

abstract: The project manager opened the kickoff meeting, introduced herself, and each team member introduced their role.

The project manager presented the project: a wearable step counter for seniors aged roughly sixty-five and up, to sell for 35 euros with a maximum production cost of 15 euros per unit including everything in the box, aimed mainly at the European market.

In a first-impressions round the team agreed that the device needs a large display with big, readable numbers. The industrial designer proposed a clip worn at the hip for accuracy, while the user interface designer preferred a wristband for ease of use; the choice was postponed to the next meeting.

The marketing expert suggested fall detection, but the project manager parked the idea because of the budget. The user interface designer offered to research existing step counters for seniors, but the marketing expert took over this task as it fits the marketing role.
The project manager distributed tasks for the functional design meeting, which follows in about thirty minutes, where each member will give a short presentation.
actions: The marketing expert will research existing step counters for seniors, including what they look like and what they cost.
The user interface designer will work on the interface and functional design (display, buttons, number of functions) and will bring rough sketches of the display.
The industrial designer will investigate the working design (sensor, battery) and what clip versus wristband means for the sensor.
The project manager will send an email with information about the next meeting and circulate the minutes.
Checking the total cost of the device (strap, packaging and so on) against the 15-euro limit was mentioned, but nobody took this on.
decisions: The step counter will have a large display with big, readable numbers, with the step count as the main element.
The choice between a clip and a wristband is deferred to the next meeting.
The marketing expert, not the user interface designer, will do the research on existing products.
problems: It is unresolved whether the device is worn as a clip at the hip (more accurate) or as a wristband (easier to put on).
Fall detection was suggested but may not fit within the 15-euro production cost; it was parked.
Battery life is a concern since seniors do not want to charge daily; a long-life coin battery was suggested but not decided.
No one has been assigned to check the total cost of all parts against the 15-euro budget.
The product has no name yet.

Bring rough sketches of the display to the next meeting.
Investigate the working design: which sensor and battery to use; present at the next meeting.
Check what wearing the device as a clip versus a wristband means for the sensor.
Send an email with information about the next meeting and circulate the minutes of this meeting.
